plan.english: Dawn, daughter of Sky, grow light!

notes: Ved. uṣo ví ucha duhitar divaḥ 'Dawn, shine forth, daughter of Heaven' (RV 1.48.1), the vocative of the title; Greek has the vocative Διὸς θύγατερ (to Aphrodite, Il. 5.348) and of Eos only δῖα < *diw-yā 'of Zeus' (Od. 9.151); West reconstructs pre-Homeric *Diwós tʰugátēr of Dawn. Interpolated: the verb, the -sḱé- present of *h₂wes- 'become light' (Ved. ucchati; Lith. aušta 'it dawns' is the same root but not in a cited passage).

plan.english: Being born, the Dawns shine.

notes: The dawn is a birth: Ved. uṣáso jā́yamānāḥ 'the Dawns as they are born' (RV 6.52.4) and bhānty uṣásaḥ 'the Dawns shine' (6.65.2); Homer's Eos is ἠριγένεια 'early-born' and φάνη 'appeared' (bʰeh₂-n-, Il. 1.477). The Vedic plural 'Dawns' is kept. ǵenh₁- is shared as a root (Ved. jā́yamāna-, a -ye- present; Gk -γένεια); the participle uses the reduplicated present middle (Gk γιγνόμενος).

plan.english: Dawn, immortal one, shine!

notes: Ved. úṣo ... ví bhāhi 'Dawn, shine forth' (RV 3.61.2) with the root of Homeric φάε ... Ἠώς 'Dawn shone' (Od. 14.502); Dawn is ajárā amŕ̥tā 'unageing, immortal' (RV 1.113.13), and Bacchylides uses the cognate ἄμβροτος of her (17.42; cited from West 2007 ch. 5 in its lemma form, not verifiable locally). 'Unageing' has no usable lexeme and is left out.

plan.english: Yoke the horses, Dawn!

notes: Ved. yukṣvá ... áśvān ... uṣaḥ 'yoke the (red) horses, Dawn' (RV 1.92.15); in the Odyssey Athena holds back Dawn and does not let her yoke (ζεύγνυσθ’) her swift-footed horses (23.244–246). Ved. aruṇā́n 'red' and Gk ὠκύποδας 'swift-footed' differ and are left out. Aorist imperative after Ved. yukṣvá (s-aorist).

plan.english: The Dawns bring light to mortals.

notes: Dawn rises 'to bring light to immortals and mortals' (Il. 11.1f. ἵν’ ἀθανάτοισι φόως φέροι ἠδὲ βροτοῖσι); the Vedic Dawns are jyótir bhárantīḥ 'bringing light' (RV 10.35.5) and give to mortal man (mártyāya, 6.65.3; Ved. mártya- is *mr̥t-yo-, Gk βροτός *mr̥tó-). 'Light' follows the Greek φόως (root *bʰeh₂-; Ved. jyótis- is another word): interpolated.

plan.english: Dawn was seen.

notes: Vedic Dawn 'has been seen' (uṣā́ adarśi, RV 7.77.3; práty adr̥śran, 7.78.3) and is darśatā́ 'a sight to behold'; Hesiod's Dawn is πολυδερκής 'much-seeing' (Th. 451, cited from West 2007 ch. 5), the same root *derḱ-. The Vedic aorist passive is rendered with the middle aorist.

plan.english: Dawn shines widely.

notes: Ved. urviyā́ ví bhāti 'she shines out widely' (RV 1.92.9; 6.64.2, of Uṣas) has the elements of the Greek name Εὐρυφάεσσα (εὐρυ- + φα-, Hymn. Hom. 31.2), which Campanile derives from a formula *'broad-shining Dawn' (West 2007 ch. 5). Ved. urviyā́ is an instrumental of urú- used as an adverb: rendered as the instrumental neuter of h₁wérHus. In the hymn Euryphaessa has become Dawn's mother (Eos is named at 31.6), so h₂éwsōs as the one who shines widely is Vedic only and is not counted as secure.

plan.english: The shining Dawns gave birth to the Sun.

notes: Ved. uṣáso vibhātī́r ájījanan sū́ryam 'the shining Dawns have given birth to the Sun' (RV 7.78.3). In Greek the Sun's mother is Theia, who 'bore great Helios ... and Eos' (Hes. Th. 371–374), or Euryphaessa 'broad-shining' (Hymn. Hom. 31.2), whom West takes to be Dawn herself forgotten as such. Shared: ǵenh₁- (ájījanan, γείνατο), the Sun, and *bʰeh₂- 'shine' (vibhātī́ḥ, -φάεσσα). h₂éwsōs as mother is Vedic only: interpolated. The Hesiodic forms are cited from the standard text, not verifiable locally (West quotes Th. 371 Ἠέλιόν τε μέγαν).

plan.english: Up goes the great Sun.

notes: Ved. súvar mahát (RV 3.2.7; neuter, like PIE *sóh₂wl̥), Sū́riyo ... mahó (2.23.2) = Hesiod's Ἠέλιόν τε μέγαν (Th. 19, 371). 'Up goes' is Vedic (úd eti, RV 7.63.2, of Sūrya's banner; 7.60.2 of Sūrya): interpolated.

plan.english: The swift Sun shines.

notes: The Sun is 'swift' with cognate adjectives: AV 13.2.2 āśúm ... sū́ryam, Mimnermus ὠκέος Ἠελίοιο (fr. 11a.1, 14.11); both cited from West 2007 ch. 5 (no local corpus). The verb *bʰeh₂- 'shine' is interpolated.

plan.english: The Sun is the watcher of gods and men.

notes: Helios is θεῶν σκοπὸς ἠδὲ καὶ ἀνδρῶν 'watcher of gods and men' (Hymn. Dem. 62); Sūrya is spáś- víśvasya jágataḥ 'spy of all that moves' (RV 4.13.3) and nr̥cákṣas- 'men-watching' (7.60.2). Ved. spáś- = PIE spéḱs; Gk σκοπός is an o-grade derivative of the same root (Kuhn's equation). *h₂nḗr: Gk ἀνδρῶν, Ved. nr̥- in the compound. 'Gods' is interpolated (Gk θεῶν; Ved. devā́nām only in other passages, e.g. 'eye of the gods' 7.76.1).

plan.english: The Sun goes up over the earth, looking at mortals.

notes: RV 7.60.2: 'this Sūrya, the men-watcher, goes up over the earth (abhí jmán) ..., looking at (páśyan) the straight and the crooked among mortals (márteṣu)'; Helios 'leapt up' (Od. 3.1) to shine for 'mortal men' (βροτοῖσιν, 3.3) and is the σκοπός of gods and men (Hymn. Dem. 62). Ved. páśyant- is the participle of *spéḱ-ye-; Gk σκοπός shares the root. Interpolated: úd and h₁ey- 'go up' (Vedic) and 'over the earth' (Ved. jmán; Gk ἐπὶ ... ἄρουραν is another word). Ved. márta- = *mr̥tó-, Gk βροτός.

plan.english: The Sun, going up, shines.

notes: Ved. sū́ra úditaḥ vibhā́ti 'the Sun, risen, shines forth' (RV 10.121.6); Helios 'leapt up ... to shine' (φαείνοι, Od. 3.1f.), φαίνω being the n-present of *bʰeh₂-. Interpolated: úd and the participle of h₁ey- (Ved. úd-ita-, a past participle; the engine has the present participle), since Gk ἀνόρουσε is another verb.

theme: The Sun's motion: wheel and steeds (West 2007 ch. 5)

plan.english: The Sun turns the wheel.

notes: The Sun's wheel: Ved. cakrám of Sūrya (eleven times; RV 2.11.20 'as Sūrya sets his wheel rolling', ávartayat), Greek ἡλίου κύκλος (Aesch. Pers. 504 etc.; Eur. El. 464f., cited from West 2007 ch. 5), and in the Edda the elves call the sun fagrahvél 'fair wheel' (Alvíssmál 16, beside sól and sunna). All three continue *kʷékʷlos and *sóh₂wl̥ (Gk ἥλιος from *seh₂wel-iyos). Interpolated: the causative wortéye- 'turn' (Ved. vartáya-, Vedic only in these passages); present for the habitual.

theme: The Sun's motion: wheel and steeds (West 2007 ch. 5)

plan.english: The horse draws the wheel of the Sun.

notes: 'The wheel of Sūrya that Etaśa draws (váhati), yoked in harness' (RV 7.63.2); 'one horse draws' the one-wheeled car (1.164.2); Euripides' shield shows 'the Sun's shining wheel on winged mares' (El. 464f., from West 2007 ch. 5), which West reads as the old horse-drawn wheel. Interpolated: wéǵʰe- 'draw, convey' (Ved. váhati only). West notes the horse-and-wheel image need not be Proto-Indo-European in date.

theme: The Sun's motion: wheel and steeds (West 2007 ch. 5)

plan.english: The horses of the Sun have taken their stand in the sky.

notes: 'The bay horses of Sūrya ... have mounted the back of heaven' (RV 1.115.3, diváḥ ... pr̥ṣṭhám asthuḥ); the goddesses find Helios before his horses (Hymn. Dem. 62f.); the Avestan Sun is 'swift-horsed' (Y. 16.4). Ved. pr̥ṣṭhá- 'back' has no usable lexeme; 'in the sky' (locative of *dyḗws) and the aorist of steh₂- (Ved. asthuḥ) are interpolated. Hymn. Dem. 63 ἵππων is cited from the standard text, not verifiable locally.

plan.english: The Sun is the eye of Sky.

notes: Macrobius reports that 'antiquity' called the sun Iouis oculus; the sun and moon are 'the two eyes of Dyaus' (RV 1.72.10, divó ... akṣī́), lexically = Διὸς ὄσσε (Il. 14.286); West 2007 ch. 4 n. 25, ch. 5. Interpolated: *sóh₂wl̥ as subject (Latin sol in Macrobius' context only; Vedic has no sun word in the stanza) and the copula.

theme: The Daughter of the Sun (West 2007 ch. 5)

plan.english: The daughter of the Sun stood on the chariot.

notes: Ved. duhitā́ sū́ryasya 'the daughter of the Sun' mounts the Aśvins' chariot (RV 1.116.17, ā́ ... rátham ... atiṣṭhat); Lith. Sáulės dukrýtė / Sáules dukte, a byword for a paragon (Brodowski, in Mannhardt 1936: 614; West 2007 ch. 5). Lith. saulė is *seh₂ul-yeh₂, a derivative of the sun word. Interpolated: the chariot (Hroth₂ós, Ved. rátha-) and the aorist of steh₂- (Ved. atiṣṭhat is an imperfect).

plan.english: The cows of the Sun are many.

notes: The Sun's cattle: 'there many cattle of Helios graze' (Od. 12.127f.; the 350 cows of the year, West 2007 ch. 5); 'Sūrya with his rays has released the cows' (RV 7.36.1). Interpolated: polh₁ús 'many' (Gk πολλαί only) and the copula.

plan.english: May we live and see the Sun.

notes: To live is to see the sun: Ved. jīváse sū́ryaṃ dr̥śé 'to live, to see the Sun' (RV 10.57.4), jīvā́ḥ ... paśyema 'may we, living, see (you), Sun' (10.37.7); Homer ζώει καὶ ὁρᾷ φάος ἠελίοιο 'lives and sees the light of the sun' (Il. 18.61), ζῶντος καὶ ... δερκομένοιο 'living and seeing' (Il. 1.88). *gʷih₃w- and *derḱ- are shared as roots (Gk ζάω is a different present formation). Optative 1st pl after Ved. paśyema.

theme: The Sun's motion: wheel and steeds (West 2007 ch. 5)

plan.english: The Sun drives along the great track.

notes: Ved. mahó ájmasya 'the great drive' (RV 4.53.4, of Savitr̥'s course) = Gk μέγας ὄγμος, the moon's orbit in Hymn. Hom. 32.11 and the sun's path in Aratus 749 (West 2007 ch. 5; Watkins 1995: 16). Ved. ájma- (*h₂éǵ-mn̥) and Gk ὄγμος (*h₂óǵ-mos) are the same root. Interpolated: the Sun (Vedic has Savitr̥, Greek the Moon), the verb h₂eǵ- 'drive' (the root of both nouns).
